Open TabTools and click a site under Suggestions, or right-click within a web page and choose Close site tabs. This closes that site’s tabs across your regular windows, including the one you are on. Pinned tabs stay open unless you turn that off in Settings.

Search by keyword or domain

Type a word to list the tabs whose titles or addresses contain it, or a site such as youtube.com to list that site and its subdomains. Check the list, then press Enter or choose Close.

Clear inactive tabs

Click Inactive to see the tabs you have not used for a while, with the time since each was last used. Choose how long counts as inactive, from 30 minutes to 1 week, then close the ones listed. Pinned, playing and current tabs stay open.

Add to Chrome

  1. Add it to your browser

    Open the Chrome, Firefox, or Edge store page and add the free extension.

  2. Open TabTools

    Click the TabTools icon in your browser’s extensions menu to see site suggestions and quick actions.

  3. Close a site or sort your tabs

    Click a site under Suggestions to close its tabs, or choose Sort tabs to bring tabs from the same site together.

Your tab data stays
in your browser.

The TabTools extension processes tab information on your device. Settings and cleanup statistics stay in your browser’s local storage. The extension has no accounts, analytics, advertising, or external database.

Read the privacy policy

Common questions.

Browsers, cleanup, and privacy.

Is TabTools free?

Yes. TabTools is free to use. No account is needed.

Which browsers can I use it with?

TabTools is available for Chrome, Firefox, and Microsoft Edge. To add it on your computer, use the browser links on this page to open the right store.

How do I close tabs from the same website?

Right-click within a web page and choose “Close site tabs,” or open TabTools and click the site under Suggestions. This closes that site’s tabs across your regular windows, including the one you are on. Pinned tabs stay open unless you turn that off in Settings. You can also type a keyword or a site in the popup and close the tabs it lists.

Can I remove duplicates or clear inactive tabs?

Yes. Choose Close duplicates to remove repeated pages. Click Inactive to review the tabs you have not used for a while, then close the ones listed. Nothing closes until you choose to.

Does TabTools collect or share my data?

The extension processes tab information locally and does not send it to the developer or third parties. Settings and cleanup statistics stay on your device. The working popup on this page runs in your browser on sample tabs and never reads your own. The browser stores this site links to have their own privacy policies.

Can I undo a cleanup?

After you close tabs from the TabTools popup, Undo appears there for a few seconds and brings them back. It goes when the popup closes. After that, use your browser’s recently closed tabs to reopen pages.
